text: Identify functions of financial intermediaries, including investment bankers and dealers.
Identify components, terms, and mechanisms related to primary and secondary markets.
Recognize the characteristics and taxation of a given type of cash or cash equivalent.
Assess how investors' tax obligations are impacted by capital gains and losses, dividends, and wash sales.
Recognize terminology, characteristics, and sources of risk of debt securities.
Calculate the conversion value, investment value, investment premium, conversion premium, and downside risk of convertible securities.
Analyze bond portfolio immunization, bond swaps, bond ladders, bond barbells, and bond bullets.
Evaluate investor profiles when recommending appropriate fixed-income securities for purchase.
Evaluate the investment implications of yield curves.
Recognize terminology and characteristics of preferred stock.
Examine the characteristics and types of common stock.
Analyze the impact of different types of cash and stock distributions on shareholders and on the company.
Examine the characteristics, structure, types, and objectives of open- and closed-end mutual funds, unit investment trusts, and separately managed accounts.
Examine the characteristics and objectives of exchange-traded funds, hedge funds, and guaranteed investment contracts.
Calculate the average cost per share of a mutual fund using various averaging techniques.
Analyze mutual fund data to determine critical factors in selecting funds for investment.
Assess the relationship between interest rates and bond prices.
Evaluate the concepts of duration and convexity in order to determine the estimated change in price of a bond.
Evaluate the concepts associated with fundamental and technical analysis and how they relate to modern portfolio theory principles.
Assess the impact of financial leverage on a company's financial performance and on the valuation of a company's stock.
Calculate the intrinsic value of a stock using various stock valuation techniques.
Compute various valuation metrics to determine if a security warrants a purchase.
Examine forms of ownership, valuation, and taxation of investment real estate.
Evaluate the various types of option investments.
Evaluate the effective use of options as speculative investments and as hedging instruments.
Describe the terminology, characteristics, uses, and taxation of futures.
Evaluate tangible asset investments.
Assess the risks, advantages, and disadvantages of investing in foreign securities.
Analyze the effect of exchange rate changes on foreign security returns.
Recognize terminology related to the analysis of risk and return in portfolio construction and management.
Differentiate among the various sources of risk in investments, both systematic and unsystematic.
Calculate beta and weighted beta and describe their application with regard to the construction of an investment portfolio.
Calculate the standard deviation and mean return of a single asset, and understand how the range of returns is calculated within one, two, and three standard deviations.
Calculate the coefficient of variation, and understand its application.
Evaluate covariance and the correlation coefficient in order to determine a portfolio's standard deviation.
Calculate the coefficient of determination, and understand its application.
Calculate various measures of investment returns.
Evaluate the common types of performance measurement.
Examine the relationships among various indicators of security returns.
Compute the current yield, yield to maturity, yield to call, and taxable equivalent yield of fixed-income securities.
Evaluate the assumptions of modern portfolio theory, including the development of indifference curves and the efficient frontier.
Analyze capital market theory, the capital market line, the capital asset pricing model (CAPM), and the security market line.
Identify the three forms of the efficient market hypothesis (EMH).
Appraise efficient market hypothesis concepts as they relate to other investment theories.
Identify the components of the investment policy statement (IPS).
Appraise the relative attractiveness of investments during various interest rate and economic cycles.
Critique asset allocation methodologies to select investment portfolios according to modern portfolio theory principles.
Evaluate the methods clients and financial planners use to manage crisis events with severe financial consequences.
